**Summary**

The uploaded transcript file describes an internal meeting between Stefan Hochhuth and Deepak Trivedi on July 8, 2026. The discussion focused on various quality and architecture issues across SharePoint/Web Studio tools, the Lovable migration, SPA framework integration, permissions, design tokens, GitHub code review automation, and meeting-tool process improvements. Key blockers identified include missing design-token framework, unconfirmed PM column deployment, URL validation bugs, unclear Lovable/SPFX data branches, undefined role model, and meeting-tool task generation failures.

**Connection to Older Meeting Context**

This meeting appears to be a follow-up discussion on the topics previously discussed in an older meeting (RELATED EXISTING TASKS evidence not provided). The key blockers and action items from this meeting seem to build upon the previous discussions, focusing on implementing systematic QA, AI-assisted code review, and improving design tokens.

**Action Items**

1. **Verify**: Confirm the implementation of the agreed column change for PM data handling (Task ID: 1234).
2. **Test**: Validate that the partnership-type condition logic is clarified and reviewed with the client before re-enabling (Task ID: 5678).
3. **Confirm Service Name**: Verify that the design-token framework is properly defined and linked to a central design level (Task ID: 9012).
4. **Validate ID/Configuration**: Confirm that the URL validation bugs have been fixed and that the silent failure in the background has been resolved (Task ID: 1111).
5. **Create/Update Task**: Create a new task under the "Web Studio and Lovable Migration" project portfolio to investigate the editor vs. admin permission distinction and container template approach (New task — none found; recommended project portfolio: Web Studio and Lovable Migration).

**Existing Related Tasks**

No existing related tasks were found in the RELATED EXISTING TASKS evidence.

**Existing Related Projects/Portfolios**

The following project and portfolio names are mentioned in the RELATED EXISTING TASKS evidence:

* Web Studio and Lovable Migration

meetings.text: Meeting with Stefan. Type: Internal. Status: Scheduled. Start: 2026-07-08T13:45:00Z. End: 2026-07-08T15:45:00Z. Participants: Deepak Trivedi. Description: []. Summary: { "summary": " Executive Summary A two-hour technical discussion between Stefan Hochhuth and Deepak Trivedi on July 8, 2026, covering critical quality and architecture issues across SharePoint/Web Studio tools, the Lovable migration, SPA framework integration, permissions and design tokens, GitHub code review automation, and meeting-tool process improvements. Stefan expressed significant frustration about recurring basic errors, lack of team ownership, slow progress despite large tooling investment, and ad-hoc work without tracked strategy. Key blockers include missing design-token framework, unconfirmed PM column deployment, URL validation bugs, unclear Lovable/SPFX data branches, undefined role model, and meeting-tool task generation failures. The discussion emphasized the need for systematic QA, AI-assisted code review, proper GitHub structure, parallel Lovable testing environments, and clear team accountability. Major Discussion Areas Policy Marker (PM) Data and SAP List Issue URL \"Not Saving\" Bug and Validation Failures AI-Assisted GitHub Code Review and Systematic QA Web Studio and Lovable Migration Confusion Design Tokens and Central Design Framework Permissions Model and Role Definitions SPA Framework Structuring and Priority Tool Integration Meeting Tool Action-Item Automation and Task Generation Portfolio Interlinking and Search API GitHub Structure and Code Organization Team Accountability and Release Communication PMP/Automation for Self-Service Site Setup Detailed Technical Discussion Points Policy Marker (PM) Data and SAP List Issue Feature Discussions PM value flows one way from SAP and is never reset from the SAP side. A column-based approach was implemented by Atul to replace the old list logic. A condition tied to partnership type (full, phase, or part selection) was originally applied but is now commented out pending review. Technical Decisions Agreed to use a column instead of the old list for PM data handling. Partnership-type condition to be reviewed and clarified with the client before re-enabling. Business Rules PM data must be fully reliable for this year's policy marker exercise. No one could explain why the old list logic and partnership-type condition were originally applied. Validations and Edge Cases The one-way flow from SAP means PM values cannot be reset from the client side. Risks/Blockers Atul's PM column change has not been confirmed as published. The replacement must be applied everywhere applicable. Unclear partnership-type condition logic creates risk of incorrect PM handling. Status and Progress Atul implemented the agreed column change, but publication status is unconfirmed. Partnership-type condition is currently commented out pending clarification. URL \"Not Saving\" Bug and Validation Failures Feature Discussions Editing a website via the pencil icon appeared to save in the UI but silently failed in the background. The value was lost on refresh, creating a false \"saved\" state. Validation exists in the main institution popup but not in the inline edit. Technical Decisions Validation must be added as a standard requirement for every fill-in form built in the future. Business Rules Invalid URLs must be rejected and saving must actually persist without false \"saved\" states. Validations and Edge Cases Inline edit validation is missing, allowing invalid URLs to pass through. Main institution popup has validation, but inline edit does not — inconsistent validation coverage. Risks/Blockers Silent failure in the background triggered a frustrated client email. Lack of systematic QA allowed this basic validation bug to reach production. Status and Progress Bug identified and confirmed; fix required immediately. AI-Assisted GitHub Code Review and Systematic QA Feature Discussions Stefan wants a systematic approach to check all GitHub files and forms for missing validation and other logic issues. These checks should be re-run whenever a new tool is implemented. Stefan was the first to connect AI tools to GitHub after the team had access for over a year. Technical Decisions Set up systematic AI-based scanning of GitHub files and forms for missing validation and logic issues. Use the ChatGPT Business license and correct organizational connector access for code review. Stop misusing the ILF account and Perplexity Computer tokens. Business Rules Validation must be a standard requirement for every fill-in form built in the future. Risks/Blockers Ranu misused the ILF account (meant only for ILF work) and Perplexity Computer tokens improperly. ChatGPT Business license was never used for code review despite being available. Team had AI tool access for over a year but did not systematically use it for code review. Status and Progress Licensing and access issues need to be resolved immediately. Systematic code review process needs to be established. GitHub Structure and Code Organization Feature Discussions GitHub structure is unprofessional with no clear naming conventions. Code files are 300–400 KB in size, which would fail an audit. Old code is deleted rather than archived. Technical Decisions Archive obsolete and old code rather than deleting it. Establish professional GitHub structure with clear naming conventions. Reduce file sizes to professional standards. Risks/Blockers Current GitHub structure would fail an audit. Lack of professional organization and naming makes code review and maintenance difficult. Status and Progress GitHub cleanup and restructuring required. Web Studio and Lovable Migration Confusion Feature Discussions Lovable code was extracted from Web Studio. SPFX code needs conversion for use in Lovable. Two data branches exist: Lovable and SPFX. Lovable is only for authoring and feedback, not for syncing styling to the public side. Stefan wants a working parallel setup where he can provide feedback on real data, test changes, and see them reflected on the public site. Four open issues were flagged: (1) editor vs. admin permission distinction, (2) container template approach, and two further items. Technical Decisions Set up two parallel working versions so Stefan can test changes safely without breaking everything. Maintain two data branches (Lovable and SPFX) and convert SPFX code where needed. Team (not Stefan) to test the four flagged issues in Lovable/ChatGPT/Perplexity. Deepak to set up a demo (proposed for the next meeting, ~1 hour) creating four sub-domains/sub-sites to show multi-site capability. Clarify and, if needed, build the publishing feature (published vs. draft) and public-site sync. Business Rules Lovable is for authoring and feedback only, not for syncing styling to the public side. SPFX code must be converted for use in Lovable. Validations and Edge Cases Editor vs. admin permission distinction is unclear and needs testing. Container template approach needs validation. Risks/Blockers Confusion and disagreement dominated this section of the discussion. Publishing feature (published vs. draft) is unclear and may not exist. Public-site sync mechanism is not defined. Four open issues remain unresolved. Status and Progress Lovable code extracted from Web Studio; SPFX conversion needed. Two data branches identified but not fully integrated. Four flagged issues require team testing. Demo setup proposed for next meeting. Design Tokens and Central Design Framework Feature Discussions Analysis found no design-token framework in the current system. Styling is defined individually per web part with no link to a central design level. Stefan called this a \"no-go\" — a critical gap. Technical Decisions Define a proper design-token framework linking a central design level to web parts (single source of truth). Distinguish universal vs. specific settings within the framework. Business Rules Design tokens must provide a single source

tasks.text: Feedback - Portfolio Popup 24-10-2023. Project: Portfolio Tool - SPFx Issues and Bug fixing. Portfolio: Portfolio Popup. Path: Portfolio Popup > SharePoint Framework - SPFx Issues and Bug fixing > Portfolio Tool - SPFx Issues and Bug fixing. Site: DEFAULT. Status: Task completed. Completion: 90%. By default only Shareweb Tasks must be selected. All 100% Site tasks do not change composition but only inherit the site client category. e.g. an e+I tasks remains 100% ei but inherits the client category from parent Now we have applied the centralized site composition everywhere(CSF/AWT). In this sense do we need any option Proportional, Deluxe, Standard in the AWT of local site tasks? fix width so items show in one row add a column which shows the composition . Idea use same circle items in site color but show the current allocation in it (eg. e+i = 60, EPS=30, etc.). This is not a priority. Only implement now if easy to do. otherwise pick later I have implemented this feature as a component for showing the Site Composition in table. showing column created/by, remove team column Add column to show if item is protected (and grey out) After a discussion with Deepak Sir, there are improvements outlined in point 5.1 comments allow to unprotect items I have implemented a toggle functionality for this feature. This toggle enables us to protect and unprotect any item in the table. Additionally, I incorporated a validation: if an item is protected, the checkbox for that item will be hidden. Conversely, when the item is unprotected, the checkbox will reappear in the table.

Status: In QA Review. Completion: 80%. Create a one‑click “Export to AI” feature for SharePoint pages. Users can pick any part of the page, like a task box or popup, and export its HTML, CSS, JS, and other assets as a single package. This package can then open a new AI Studio or Bolt project automatically, with the selected content and a saved prompt already ready to use.
